title: Practice: Angles of Elevation and Depression

questions.stem: A person stands 50 m from the base of a tower. The angle of elevation to the top of the tower is 32 degrees. What is the height of the tower to 1 decimal place?
From the top of a 40 m cliff, the angle of depression to a boat is 25 degrees. How far is the boat from the base of the cliff? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: The angle of depression from the cliff top equals the angle of elevation from the boat (alternate angles). tan(25) = 40 / distance. Distance = 40 / tan(25) = 40 / 0.4663 = 85.8 m (1 d.p.).

questions.stem: A kite is flying 30 m above the ground. The string is 50 m long and taut. What is the angle of elevation from the person holding the string to the kite? Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
From the top of a lighthouse 60 m above sea level, the angles of depression to two boats in a line are 28 degrees and 45 degrees. How far apart are the boats? Give your answer to the nearest metre.
questions.explanation: Distance to nearer boat: 60 / tan(45) = 60 / 1 = 60 m. Distance to farther boat: 60 / tan(28) = 60 / 0.5317 = 112.8 m. Distance between boats = 112.8 - 60 = 52.8, approximately 53 m.

questions.stem: A tree casts a shadow 12 m long when the angle of elevation of the sun is 55 degrees. How tall is the tree to 1 decimal place?
